desc: San Francisco maker of high-resolution digital lidar sensors for robotics, industrial automation, smart infrastructure and automotive uses.
markets: Sells lidar sensors to customers in North America, Europe and Asia across industrial, robotics and automotive markets.
rationale: Sensor technology brand with global industrial customers; F1 offers technology showcase and B2B hospitality, though consumer brand is limited.
changed: Merged with Velodyne in 2023

name: Telefonica Emisiones
desc: Financing vehicle of the Spanish telecoms group Telefonica that issues bonds and other debt instruments for the group.
markets: Spanish group debt issuer with no customers of its own; the parent Telefonica operates in Europe and Latin America.
rationale: Debt-issuing vehicle with no brand or customers; any partnership would be through the parent, so fit is minimal.

name: Glydways
desc: South San Francisco developer of autonomous transit systems using small driverless vehicles running on dedicated guideways.
markets: US-based developer building first deployments with transport agencies; no verified international operations.
rationale: Pre-revenue public transit technology developer selling to government agencies, with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: MicroVision
desc: Washington developer of laser beam scanning and lidar sensors, including MOVIA lidar for automotive driver assistance.
markets: US-based with a German engineering operation from the 2023 Ibeo asset purchase; targets global automotive customers.
rationale: Lidar technology company with small revenue; F1 offers technology showcase, but limited consumer brand and budget.

name: UzAuto Motors
desc: Uzbekistan main automaker, headquartered in Tashkent, producing Chevrolet-branded cars such as Cobalt, Gentra, Tracker and Onix under licence.
markets: Produces cars mainly for the Uzbek market; export volumes to neighbouring countries not verified.
rationale: Dominant local carmaker with brand licensed from General Motors; F1 ties could build prestige, but market is small.
f1: Builds Chevrolet-branded cars under licence from General Motors, owner of the Cadillac F1 team.

name: AutoStore
desc: Norwegian maker of cube-based automated storage and retrieval systems for warehouses, sold through system integrator partners.
markets: Systems installed in warehouses across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, sold through integrator partners.
rationale: Global technology brand selling to retailers and logistics firms; F1 offers B2B hospitality and technology showcase.

name: Fair
desc: Former Santa Monica vehicle subscription and leasing company, founded by Scott Painter in 2016, offering flexible app-based car leases.
markets: Offered app-based car leases to US drivers; scaled back sharply after 2022.
rationale: Former consumer car-lease start-up with little verified current activity; an F1 partnership is very unlikely.

name: Mitsubishi Motors
desc: Japanese automaker producing the Outlander, Eclipse Cross, Pajero and Triton, with large sales in Southeast Asia, Australia and Europe.
markets: Sells vehicles across Southeast Asia, Australia, Europe and North America, with plants in Thailand, Indonesia and Japan.
rationale: Global automotive brand with Asia-Pacific strength; F1 could support brand awareness and electrification messaging in Asian markets.

name: UCAR
desc: Chinese chauffeured car service and mobility company, founded in 2013, providing app-based ride-hailing with company-owned vehicles and professional drivers.
markets: Operates in Chinese cities only; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic ride-hailing service with little brand marketing abroad; F1 fit is weak.

name: Zhidou
desc: Chinese small electric vehicle maker in Zhejiang, producing compact pure-electric city cars for urban buyers and ride-hailing fleets.
markets: Chinese compact EV maker; sales are domestic and current operating status is not verified.
rationale: Low-cost city EV maker with no international ambitions shown; F1 fit is weak.

name: Lime
desc: San Francisco micromobility company operating shared electric scooters and e-bikes in about 280 cities across North America, Europe and beyond.
markets: Operates in cities across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, partnering with Uber and local authorities.
rationale: Consumer micromobility brand with city reach; F1 race-city activations could help, but budgets are limited.

name: Europcar
desc: Major European car and van rental company operating Europcar, Goldcar, InterRent and other brands across many countries.
markets: Rents vehicles in Europe and, through franchisees, in many countries across other regions.
rationale: Large consumer travel brand; F1 race-weekend travel and hospitality fit rental and mobility audiences in Europe and beyond.

name: Ricarica
desc: Milan company in electric vehicle and energy sectors that operates as a charging operator offering EV charging services.
markets: Based in Italy; the input shows no international operations.
rationale: Charging operator with unverified scale; F1 electrification link and the Italian Grand Prix give some relevance.

name: Verra Mobility
desc: Arizona smart mobility technology company providing electronic toll management, violation enforcement and parking services for fleets, rental companies and governments.
markets: Serves customers in the United States and Europe, including rental fleets and municipal governments.
rationale: B2B mobility software firm with rental-car and government customers; F1 offers client hospitality, though consumer brand is limited.

name: Dana
desc: Maker of drivetrain and propulsion technology: axles, driveshafts, transmissions, e-motors, inverters and sealing and thermal-management products for vehicles.
markets: Plants and customers across North America, Europe, South America and Asia-Pacific, supplying light, commercial and off-highway vehicle makers.
rationale: Global Tier-1 supplier with technology credentials; F1 offers engineering showcase and B2B hospitality, with limited consumer brand.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to sell its Off-Highway business to Allison Transmission

name: Piaggio Group
desc: Italian maker of scooters and motorcycles, owning Piaggio, Vespa, Aprilia, Moto Guzzi and Gilera brands, plus Ape commercial vehicles.
markets: Sells in Europe, India, Asia-Pacific and the Americas, with plants in Italy, India and Vietnam.
rationale: Iconic Italian two-wheeler brands with motorsport heritage; F1 fits Aprilia and Vespa marketing in Europe and Asia.

name: Canadian Tire Corporation
desc: Canadian retailer selling automotive parts and service, sports and leisure, home and hardware products through Canadian Tire stores.
markets: Stores across Canada; operations are almost entirely Canadian.
rationale: Major consumer brand in Canada, with automotive parts and sports audiences; F1 helps through the Canadian Grand Prix, but market is single-country.

name: Electrify America
desc: Operator of the largest open DC fast-charging network for electric vehicles in the US, with over 1,000 stations.
markets: Operates fast chargers across the United States and Canada.
rationale: Charging network with consumer visibility and carmaker partners; F1 electrification message fits, backed by its parent group.
f1: Parent Volkswagen Group owns Audi, which enters F1 as a works team in 2026.

name: Mahindra Electric Automobile
desc: Electric vehicle subsidiary of Mahindra and Mahindra behind the BE 6 and XEV 9e electric SUVs on the INGLO platform.
markets: Sells electric SUVs in India; overseas export plans for the parent exist but are not verified here.
rationale: Fast-growing Indian EV brand with technology image; F1 could help brand awareness, but sales are domestic.

name: The Lion Electric
desc: Maker of zero-emission medium and heavy-duty vehicles, including LionD school buses and LionA and LionC trucks, built in Quebec.
markets: Sells school buses and trucks in Canada and the United States, with plants in Quebec and Illinois.
rationale: Fleet-focused electric vehicle maker emerging from restructuring; F1 offers little consumer or commercial value.
changed: Entered creditor protection in 2024; business sold to a Quebec investor group in 2025

name: CarTrade Tech
desc: Indian operator of online automotive marketplaces including CarWale, BikeWale, CarTrade and Shriram Automall for new, used and auction vehicles.
markets: Marketplaces serve Indian buyers and sellers; no significant verified overseas operations.
rationale: Digital consumer brand with strong Indian automotive audience; F1 could help brand awareness, but all customers are domestic.

name: Regent
desc: Rhode Island developer of all-electric seagliders, wing-in-ground-effect craft that skim above the water carrying passengers and cargo.
markets: US-based developer preparing first commercial craft; no confirmed international sales or operations.
rationale: Pre-revenue vehicle developer with innovation story; F1 technology showcase is possible, but budget is small. Not Regent Seven Seas Cruises.

name: Air-e
desc: Electricity distributor and retailer serving the Colombian Caribbean coast region, including Barranquilla, Atlantico, Magdalena and La Guajira.
markets: Regulated electricity distribution on Colombia's Caribbean coast; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated local utility with no consumer marketing need and under government intervention; weak F1 fit.
changed: Placed under government intervention by Colombia's utilities regulator in 2024

name: Carvolution
desc: Swiss car subscription provider offering new vehicles on all-inclusive monthly plans covering insurance, maintenance, tyres and registration.
markets: Serves Swiss customers only; no international operations verified so far.
rationale: Consumer subscription brand in a small single-country market; F1 offers limited relevance for its audience.

name: Fritz Winter
desc: Family-owned German foundry group producing cast iron vehicle components such as brake discs, crankshafts, engine blocks and cylinder heads.
markets: German foundry supplying vehicle makers mainly in Europe; overseas operations not verified.
rationale: B2B casting supplier with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality could suit carmaker clients, but fit is weak.

name: TI Clean Mobility
desc: Electric mobility subsidiary of Tube Investments of India, part of the Murugappa Group, making electric three-wheelers, tractors and commercial vehicles.
markets: Sells electric three-wheelers and tractors in India; no verified international operations.
rationale: Industrial group electric vehicle arm with domestic customers and little marketing need; F1 fit is weak.
